WOODS RUN DIGEST

Tuesday edition

November 17, 2026

CANADA — QUEBEC / SAWMILL OPERATIONS

Domtar to halt sawing at its Baie-Comeau mill November 20

Domtar told Quebec media that Scierie des Outardes will stop sawing on November 20 for an indefinite period. The company cited uncertainty over fibre supply and harvest planning, high fibre and freight costs, U.S. duties and weak lumber prices.

The pause reaches beyond lumber. The Journal de Québec reported that chips from the mill also go to Domtar’s Clermont pulp mill and Arbec’s Port-Cartier biofuel operation. The report did not identify replacement chip supplies or a restart date.

Le Manic: Domtar’s announcement → · Journal de Québec: chip customers →

By the Numbers

Latest available observations as of 2026-11-17. Dates and comparison periods vary by series; monthly figures remain unchanged between releases.

IndicatorLatestChange
U.S. on-highway dieselEIA U.S. on-highway diesel; taxes includedUS$6.13/galWeek of November 9, 2026; released November 10−US$0.17/gal
−2.6%Versus November 2: US$6.29/gal
Lumber futuresJanuary 2027 lumber futures (CME LBRF27)US$510.00/MBFNovember 16, 2026 settlementUnavailableNovember 9 January settlement not independently verified
Madison’s lumber indexMadison’s weekly lumber indexUS$444.00/MBFWeek ending November 13, 2026−US$5.00/MBF
−1.1% (calculated)Versus week ending November 6: US$449.00/MBF
Hardwood lumber PPIBLS WPU0812; 1982=100; not seasonally adjusted284.3 index pointsOctober 2026; released November 13−1.3 points
−0.4%Versus revised September 2026: 285.6
U.S. single-family housing startsCensus U.S. single-family starts; annualized estimate859,000 units (SAAR)September 2026; released October 20−41,000 units (SAAR)
−4.6%Versus revised August 2026: 900,000
Canadian dollarBank of Canada; Canadian dollars per U.S. dollarC$1.43 per US$1.00Daily average, November 16, 2026+C$0.00 per US$1.00
+0.3%Versus November 13: C$1.43 per US$1.00

Housing starts are annualized estimates, not actual monthly units, and are subject to revision. The hardwood PPI is an index, not a dollar price. Exchange rates are daily averages. MBF means thousand board feet. The September single-family starts monthly change has a published ±10.0-percentage-point 90.0% confidence interval and is not statistically significant. EIA’s next weekly diesel release is due November 17; the latest observation available at publication is November 9. The January lumber settlement is verified for November 16; the November 9 same-contract settlement could not be independently confirmed. Display rounding follows the approved format. Changes are calculated from unrounded observations, so rounded currency levels may look unchanged even when a small movement occurred.

Sources:
EIA U.S. on-highway diesel; taxes included
Investing.com January contract settlement
CME delivery calendar
Madison’s November 13 index
BLS hardwood lumber PPI via FRED
Census U.S. single-family starts; annualized estimate
Bank of Canada daily averages

Trade Policy Watch

U.S. Commerce’s final antidumping and countervailing duty orders on hardwood and decorative plywood from China, Indonesia and Vietnam are scheduled for Federal Register publication November 17. The orders give importers producer- and exporter-specific cash deposit tables. They also distinguish covered panels from qualifying stamped structural softwood plywood and certain panels that failed structural certification, for which Commerce directs refunds of specified deposits. The notices explain which entry dates and scope rules apply. Antidumping order and deposit tables · Countervailing duty order and scope

Working Forests

U.S. WEST — NORTHERN IDAHO / FUELS WORK

Northern Idaho plans pile burns through December

The Bureau of Land Management lists prescribed pile burning near Pinehurst and across several sites in its Cottonwood field office area through December. At Happy Trails in Adams County, the plan covers roughly 257 acres of hand piles and 338 acres of machine piles. Burn timing depends on weather, staffing and field conditions.

Bureau of Land Management: burn locations and acreages →

Action Detector

U.S. — NATIONAL FORESTS / COMMENTS DUE DECEMBER 14

Forest Service seeks comments on targeted grazing permits

A November 12 Forest Service proposal would let the agency use temporary grazing or livestock permits for stewardship work, including targeted grazing. It also proposes a framework for changing grazing in response to drought or wildfire. Written comments are due December 14; the notice gives filing instructions under RIN 0596-AD75.

Federal Register: proposal and comment instructions →

Under the Radar

THE FBS PODCAST / NOVEMBER 16 RELEASE

New FBS episode explains what state business assistance can cover

In “FBS 62 Forest Business Assistance from State Agencies,” Steve Bick walks through help forest businesses can explore before committing to equipment or an expansion. Examples include South Carolina’s timber supply and market analyses and Montana’s wood products revolving fund. The episode distinguishes advice, direct loans and grants that reimburse eligible spending.

Listen to the episode on Spotify → · Watch the episode on YouTube →

Today's Featured Resource

LiVT — Log in Vermont

LiVT is a browser app for evaluating logging-business financial results. Enter overhead, equipment, labor, production and revenue to examine profit or loss for a week or job.

Explore LiVT — Log in Vermont →
